subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a militarized cyberpunk truck design for 2077—a heavy six-wheeler with armor plating, a turret, neon glow accents, roof rack, missile pods in the cargo bed, and decals, keeping the rig simple with joints for the chassis, wheels, and turret.

Now I'm working out the dimensions (roughly 8m long, 2.8m wide, 3.2m tall) and setting up helper functions for building box-shaped parts and extruded hull sections, defining the truck's side profile with the cab toward the front and cargo bed toward the rear. Sketching hull profile coordinates...

Then the rear bed becomes a separate box extending back from the cab, with armored panels and a turret mounted on top. For materials, I'm leaning cyberpunk: dark gunmetal hull with neon magenta/cyan accents and hazard stripes, using the panelled metal paint from the clockwork kit plus a glow effect, staying within the 64-color limit.

I also need to generate several SVG textures: hazard stripes for bumpers, a neon emblem decal for the door, a HUD-style windshield glow with cyan grid lines, vent grilles, a cargo-side "KX-77" marking, glowing light bar strips, a radar screen, and tire tread detail—each applied as a textured plane positioned against the relevant hull faces.

Now I'm working out wheel placement: three axles along the z-axis with front and rear positions, wheels offset symmetrically on x, sized to match the hull's ride height, with tire cylinders rotated to the correct axis and metallic hub caps with a glowing ring accent.

Each wheel also needs bolt details, so I'm planning roughly six bolts per wheel across all six wheels, keeping total part count manageable while setting up the joint hierarchy so wheels attach correctly to the chassis bone at their respective positions and orientations.

Working out tread lugs...

Still planning body geometry...

Placing the HUD glass with a dark navy base and glowing cyan lines so it reads as armored glass rather than a flat emissive surface. For the side windows I'm adding slanted slit-style openings on the cab sides, positioned with dark tinted glass to match the armored aesthetic.

Adding door emblem decals, extruded armor skirt panels along the cab's lower sides with a hazard-striped polygon profile, and a wedge-shaped bumper plow extruded from a front-view outline.

I'm resolving the overlap by lowering the bumper outline to y 0.55-1.1 and placing headlights above at y 1.3, with two glowing rectangular units flanking a center bar near z=3.96. For the roof I'm planning a magenta light bar, a lathed sensor dome, and thin sweeping antennas.

For the rear I'm adding twin exhaust stacks behind the cab (cylinders with glowing orange tips) and sketching out the cargo bed dimensions behind the cab wall, considering a modular armored container to place on top.

Now I'm planning the rear launcher assembly: a flat deck section near the cab holding the turret base, and a raised rear section with two angled missile pods, each containing 8 glowing-tipped tubes arranged 2x4 and tilted upward-backward for a menacing silhouette.

Working out tube placement at the glowing end of each pod, then figuring out pod center positions on the deck so the angled pods sit correctly with their bottoms resting against the hull.

I need to figure out the local Z axis orientation for this bone by checking how "up" and "backward" directions interpolate between known reference cases, computing the perpendicular vector in the YZ plane that stays consistent with those boundary conditions.

Now I'm moving to the turret assembly, planning its pivot point and building it from a turret base ring and a wedge-shaped body defined by a polygon profile in the local z-y plane.

For the gun mount, I'm positioning it relative to the turret pivot and designing twin barrels as rods with a shroud radius, plus glowing cyan rail strips and coil rings to give them a railgun aesthetic.

I'm adding turret details now: a hatch box, a sensor eye cylinder with a glowing red lens, ammo box, four smoke launcher cylinders per side, and a commander cupola dome. For the joint hierarchy I'm keeping roles minimal, starting with the chassis as root and sticking mostly to plain parts rather than over-tagging roles.

I'm also planning underglow neon strips along the sides for the magenta lighting effect, and working out the bed's side armor details — texture panels with warning markings, vertical ribs, and a chamfered polygon profile extruded along the body length to give the cargo bed its angular armored shape.

Working out the normal direction for the mirrored negative-x bevel, then handling the upper slope above y=1.5 where x tapers from 1.45 to 1.2, giving a steeper outward normal for the armor panel there.

Now I'm planning the rear bed details: a hazard-textured ramp plane plus a glowing red tail-light bar, positioned at the back face with thin box geometry for the center and side lights. I'm also designing the roof rack with an alternating magenta/cyan light bar made of eight segments, and starting on the side mirror arms mounted near the cab front.

I'm now adding whip antennas on the rear roof using tapered rod geometry with glowing tip spheres, plus sketching out a radar dish on the roof built from a lathe profile outline.

For the dish, I'm defining its radius/height profile points and tilting its rotation axis so it faces up and forward, mounted via a feed rod at the joint position. I'm also considering extra deck details like cargo crates, then moving on to add thin side armor skirt plates along the vehicle's flanks.

Now I'm placing drive shaft cylinders along the underbody and figuring out side-mounted fuel tank cylinders between the front and rear axles, checking the z-gap and x-offset so the tanks don't collide with the cab's width.

Checking wheel placement against chassis height, I realize the wheels at radius 0.75 sink into the hull sides where the bed geometry sits, so I need to push the wheel centers outward in x to clear the body width — but that makes the overall truck too wide, so I'll need to scale the whole thing down.

I settle on narrowing the hull instead: a tapered bed cross-section with half-widths around 1.0-1.2, and wheel centers at roughly ±1.45 with width 0.5, giving a total vehicle width near 3.4 which feels proportionate. Now I'm adjusting the decal x-offsets to match the new narrower bed geometry at each height.

Placing fender boxes over the wheels at y1.62, sizing them to span from the cab/bed edge outward and touch the body sides, plus a thin vertical lip at the outer edge for detail.

Checking the vertical stack: tires sit at y0 with radius 0.75, roof tops out near 3.0, and the turret with light bar reaches about 3.15-3.2, giving a total height near 3.4 before antennas push it toward 5.

Now I'm working out the hull paint — thinking a panelled iron texture feels too dark, so I'm sketching a custom camo-style base using mottled dark greens/grays with panel overlay and a muddy wrap near the bottom.

Writing paint composition code...

Now I'm planning out accent colors as constants (dark steel, neon cyan, magenta, yellow, red, orange) keeping the flat palette small, then starting on the texture definitions beginning with a hazard pattern.

Writing hazard stripe, emblem, HUD windshield, side vent, and label plate SVGs...

Only neon lines glow; the emblem decal stays unglowed while circuit and HUD elements keep their glow. I'm adding door seams and tiny handle boxes to the cab, plus sensor pod clusters, cable bundle sweeps along the cab top, side pistons, and stacked cargo crates with texture labels on the deck, and giving the headlights their own glowing boxes.

Now I'm working out the plow bumper geometry: merging cones for teeth along the front edge, positioning a hazard-stripe plane on the bumper face, and placing window frame boxes around the slit windows plus an under-bumper glow strip. I'm also figuring out the z-depth math so the bumper extends past the cab front without clipping, then placing the grille vents and front lights at the right height on the cab face.

Starting to write the builder code for the truck now...

Adding box and cylinder helpers...

Adding wheel hub, rim, hubcap, bolts, and tread lugs...

Writing wheel geometry helper...

Still building wheel and hub geometry... I'm simplifying by skipping spoke rings and brake discs, then roughing in the chassis frame with axle cylinders, differential boxes, a driveshaft, and underglow strips along the underside.

Now I'm shaping the cab by extruding a profile outline along the body's length with beveled edges, keeping it centered on the chassis and colored to match the hull.

Next I'm working out the bed extrusion, positioning it so it overlaps slightly with the back of the cab to avoid any visible gap, then sketching the bed's cross-section outline with widened top edges.

For the deck I'm adding a raised rim border with rails along the top edges plus supporting ribs. I'm placing the turret at a height and position that fits between the cab and the launcher without colliding, then adding ammo crates in the space just in front of the turret.

Checking clearances between turret body, crates, and launcher pods, I decide to skip the fuel drums and extra roof details since space is too tight, and move on to setting the turret's pivot point and local coordinate system for its yaw joint.

Still defining turret geometry...

Adding barrel geometry now...

Adding a glowing sensor box on the turret top with a red lens, plus a rear antenna, side shield emblems on the turret cheeks, and now placing a radar joint near the cab roof.

I'm positioning the light bar, radar mast and dish, a hemisphere sensor dome with glow lens on the right side, tilted rod antennas, and a beacon, then starting on exhaust stacks.

Checking exhaust stack placement next to the cab back wall, sizing the cylinder with a glowing orange rim cap and heat shield box, and making sure the stacks clear the turret radius.

Now I'm working out the windshield glass geometry, positioning a sloped plane between two points on the cab front and calculating its outward-facing normal direction.

Working out box rotation angles...

Still working out window geometry and door plate coordinates...

I need to check clearance between the door armor plate and the front wheel—they're close enough to touch slightly, so I'm trimming the plate's front edge back to around z=2.0 with a diagonal cut to avoid overlap.

Now I'm settling on the axle positions: front axle around z=2.8, rear axles around -1.35 and -2.95, checking that the bed's lower half-width clears the wheel housing. I'm laying out each wheel's bounding box and fender/arch geometry, with an outer lip piece positioned near the wheel's outer edge.

I'm adding small rear mudflaps behind the rearmost axle only, confirming their position still sits within the bed's length, then moving on to sketch the front bumper as an extruded outline with a fixed thickness.

Checking the bumper width against the front wheel span, I narrow it slightly so it clears the wheels properly, then add a hazard light plane near the bumper's top edge and start placing teeth as a row of cones angled outward.

Now I'm adding steel-colored lamp pods at the bumper's top corners with amber glow, skipping the winch and tow hooks for now, and moving on to shape the hood with vents and a slanted scoop.

For hood detailing I'm computing a function for the hood's curved surface height along the z-axis, then placing thin neon cyan rods along both sides of the hood slope to act as glowing decal lines, followed by adding a vent plane further back on the hood.

I'm also planning a textured hood vent panel with a slight slope-matched normal and tilt, plus a center ridge box for armor styling, and sketching out roof details -- a rack with four thin rail boxes, a segmented light bar, and a roof hatch -- before moving on to the cab's rear wall near the bed front.

For the truck's rear end, I'm placing a flat rectangular back door plane with tail light glow boxes positioned just below it, adjusting the door's vertical span and light placement so they don't overlap, then adding a dark rear bumper box with space reserved for a towing hitch.

I'm positioning side label decals on the lower sloped bed panels, tilted to match the slope angle so they read correctly from outside, and planning a glowing circuit panel on the upper slope with its position and normal vector calculated to sit flush against the angled surface -- skipping the rib details since fitting boxes onto the sloped geometry gets too complicated.

Instead of ribs, I'm considering scattering small rivet/stud cylinders across the hull using a surface scatter function filtered to flat side faces within a certain height range, though I'm wary it might accidentally place studs on decal areas or near the wheels.

I'm also thinking about adding greebles underneath, like cylindrical fuel tanks rotated to lie along the z-axis, positioned between the wheels so they don't collide with the front wheel's rear edge.

Still writing cable runs...

Adding magenta rod near the lower slope, checking wheel clearance at z, then placing cyan neon along the cab roof edges. I'm skipping extra cab interior details and starting the hazard texture SVG markup.

Designing more icon SVGs...

That gives me 8 textures total: HAZARD, EMBLEM, HUD, SLIT, VENT, LABEL, CIRCUIT, REAR, with varying glow intensities for the windshield, slit, vent, and circuit. For tires, I'm painting a noisy dark gradient with a dirt layer blended in near the bottom using smoothstep.

Now I'm importing metal and panelled helpers from the clockwork kit, plus glow and paint utilities from the SDK. For the hull, I'm building a mottled camo base color, then layering in a rust tint toward the bottom using noise and smoothstep, and lightening the top surface based on normal direction before passing it into the panelled geometry builder.

Writing armor plate variants...

Working out wheel coordinates and the lug placement loop around the rim, positioning each lug box radially and rotating it about the X axis so it aligns with its angular direction.

Naming wheel joints per side and index, and estimating total part count across wheels, cab, turret, and studs lands around 250, which seems reasonable. Now I'm checking the rod helper's signature for radius and color options so I use it correctly with glow effects applied to sweeps.

Setting up the joint hierarchy next: turret yaw joint off the chassis, then gun pitch off the turret, then a radar joint, each with appropriate pivot points and directions. Defining helper offsets for turret-relative positions, then placing gun ring geometry using rotated cylinders...

Now I'm adding the mantlet box, breech, and barrel rod geometry on the turret, plus a small cyan glow ring at the muzzle tip for effect. Moving on to the missile launcher pods, computing a normalized direction vector for their orientation.

Still writing tube geometry...

Avoiding setFromUnitVectors, I'll compute rotation with a simple Euler angle about X instead, deriving the angle from the direction vector's components and using it consistently for both the tube placement and the pod box orientation.

Now I'm laying out the pod's base support box and hinge cylinders beneath it, then moving on to the roof light bar made of alternating cyan/magenta glowing segments merged by color, while skipping wiper details and adding fog lights to the cab front.

I'm writing a mirror helper and vector constructor, then adding scattered stud geometry (small hex cylinders) across the bed surface filtered by normal direction, and considering similar studs on the cab while avoiding window decal areas.

I'll skip studs on the cab windows, then move to coding the turret sensor box and the radar dish using a lathe operation with a defined cross-section outline for the dish's curved profile.

Adding the feed horn rod along the dish axis, positioning the radar joint at the mast top, and tilting the dish forward with a tapered angle so it faces outward from the mast. I'm also placing antenna rods on each side with tilted positions and glowing tips.

For the small glowing tip spheres, mirrored door plates, mudflaps, and fenders, I'm checking orientation conventions for the extrusion thickness direction. I'll finalize the vehicle name as "Ares KX-77 Siege Hauler" and verify that glow effects require the right material setup.

I'm locking in the color palette with dark, steel, and gunmetal tones, then writing out the full build, keeping it thorough but not excessively long.
